## Purpose

This SOP describes the procedures for collecting, processing, and
storing soil samples for laboratory analysis. It covers field sampling
using a soil auger, sample homogenization, sieving, and subdivision
for biological assays, carbon analysis, and other soil properties
[@robertson1999; @fao2024].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All field-based soil sampling for EA Program
  research, including photovoltaic panel studies, agricultural plots,
  and restoration sites
- **Does not apply to:** Deep soil coring (> 30 cm) requiring
  mechanized equipment; contaminated site sampling requiring
  chain-of-custody protocols
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve sampling plan, ensure training compliance       |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate sampling logistics, ensure protocol
                      adherence                                           |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and process samples according to this SOP       |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sampling           |


## Definitions

- **Bulk sample:** A large, mixed sample collected from multiple
  locations within a sampling unit and combined before analysis;
  represents the average composition of the unit rather than any
  single point.
- **Composite sample:** A sample formed by combining and mixing a
  defined number of subsamples from a plot or area; reduces analytical
  cost while improving spatial representativeness; the number and
  pattern of subsamples must be recorded [@robertson1999].
- **Core (soil core):** A cylindrical soil sample extracted with a
  push-probe or hammer corer; preserves the depth profile and allows
  depth-discrete sampling; also used for bulk density determination
  (see [SOP-F402](SOP-F402-soil-bulk-density.qmd)).
- **Fine earth fraction:** Soil material passing through a 2 mm sieve;
  sand, silt, and clay particles; the standard fraction for chemical
  analysis; gravel and coarser material are removed and their mass
  fraction recorded [@robertson1999].
- **Grab sample:** A single, point-in-time sample collected from one
  location; appropriate when spatial variability is low or when
  individual point values are required; contrasted with composite
  sampling.
- **Pedogenic horizon:** A layer of soil with distinct physical,
  chemical, or biological properties developed through soil-forming
  processes; designated by letter symbols (O, A, E, B, C, R); sampled
  discretely in profile descriptions (see
  [SOP-F407](SOP-F407-soil-profile-description.qmd)).
- **Push-probe (soil probe):** A hollow stainless steel tube pushed
  into the soil by hand or with a slide hammer to collect an intact
  soil core; the standard tool for rapid depth-discrete sampling in
  fine-textured soils without large stones [@robertson1999].
- **Sampling depth increment:** A defined depth interval (e.g.,
  0--10 cm, 10--20 cm) from which soil is collected; depth increments
  must be consistent within a study for results to be comparable
  [@robertson1999].
- **Subsample:** One of the individual small samples taken from within
  a plot that are combined to form a composite; also refers to a
  representative aliquot drawn from a bulk sample for laboratory
  analysis.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Repetitive strain from augering, sharp edges on
  sieving equipment, trip hazards at field sites.
- **Biological:** Soil-borne pathogens, tick and insect exposure at
  field sites.
- **Chemical:** Potential exposure to contaminated soils at some sites.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Nitrile or latex gloves
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when sieving)

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for
general field safety procedures.


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soil auger (Dutch or bucket)          | Diameter 5--10 cm; clean between sites  |
| Push-probe (soil core sampler)        | For depth-discrete sampling              |
| Rubber mallet or slide hammer         | For driving probe into hard soils        |
| Stainless steel bowl or plastic bucket | For compositing subsamples              |
| Stainless steel sieve (2 mm)          | For fine earth fraction                  |
| Ziploc bags or Whirl-Pak bags (labeled) | For each sample                        |
| Permanent markers and labels          | Waterproof; include site, depth, date    |
| Cooler with ice                       | For biological subsamples (enzyme assays, MBC, microbial DNA) |
| Field notebook                        | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |
| GPS unit                              | Per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Isopropyl alcohol and paper towels    | For decontaminating tools between sites  |


## Sampling Design

Before sampling, confirm the sampling design with the PI and reference
[SOP-F005 Random Sampling Design](SOP-F005-random-sampling-design.qmd)
for plot layout and randomization [@robertson1999]. Record the
following in the field notebook:

- Site name and GPS coordinates
- Sampling date and personnel
- Target depth(s) or horizon(s)
- Number of subsamples per composite
- Auger/probe diameter
- Any deviations from the sampling plan


## Procedure

### Field Collection

1. Navigate to the sampling location per
   [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd).
2. Record the GPS coordinates of each sample location.
3. Inspect the surface for hazards. Clear surface litter only if
   required by the protocol; record whether litter was cleared.
4. Insert the auger or push-probe vertically to the target depth.
   For depth-increment sampling:
   - Collect the 0--10 cm increment first. Remove and place in a
     labeled sample container.
   - Re-insert the auger and collect the 10--20 cm increment. Place in
     a separate container.
   - Repeat for additional depth increments as required by the sampling
     plan.
5. For composite samples, collect subsamples at each designated
   subplot location (typically 5--10 per plot) and combine in the
   bowl or bucket before homogenizing.
6. Record the following for each sample:
   - Sample ID per the project labeling scheme
   - GPS coordinates
   - Depth increment
   - Observed soil conditions (color, texture, moisture, visible roots,
     stoniness)
   - Any anomalies (disturbance, compaction, visible contamination)

### Field Homogenization

7. Break up clods and remove surface litter, roots greater than 5 mm,
   visible rocks, and obvious debris by hand [@robertson1999].
8. Mix the soil thoroughly in the bowl or bucket until the color and
   texture appear uniform.
9. If the sample is to be composited across subsamples, combine all
   subsamples before mixing.

### Sieving (Field or Lab)

Sieving can be performed in the field (when fresh soil is required for
biological assays) or in the lab after air-drying (for chemical
analysis) [@robertson1999; @fao2024]:

1. Pass the soil through a 2 mm stainless steel sieve.
2. Weigh and record the mass of coarse fragments (> 2 mm) retained if
   the project protocol requires correction for coarse fragment content.
3. The fine earth fraction (< 2 mm) is the standard fraction for all
   chemical and biological analyses.

### Sample Subdivision for Multiple Analyses

Divide the sieved fine earth fraction into the required subsamples
before further drying or freezing [@robertson1999]:

| Subsample type        | Treatment                  | Storage        |
|:----------------------|:---------------------------|:---------------|
| Microbial biomass C/N | Field-moist; process within 24 h | Cooler 4 °C then lab |
| Enzyme assays         | Field-moist; process within 24 h or freeze | Cooler/freezer (-20 °C) |
| Mineral N (KCl)       | Field-moist or frozen; extract within 48 h | Cooler 4 °C |
| Soil moisture (gravimetric) | Field-moist           | Sealed bag     |
| Carbon/nitrogen (EA-IRMS) | Air-dry, then grind    | Room temperature |
| pH, texture, other chemical | Air-dry                | Room temperature |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Biological Subsamples
Do not freeze biological subsamples unless the analysis protocol
explicitly permits it.
:::

### Tool Decontamination Between Sites

Wipe the auger, probe, and bowl with isopropyl alcohol and let dry
before moving to the next sampling location. This prevents
cross-contamination of soils between sites and is particularly
important for sites with invasive species or contamination concerns
[@fao2024].


## Quality Control

- Collect field duplicates at a rate of 1 per 10 samples to assess
  sampling variability [@robertson1999].
- Record all deviations from the sampling plan in the field notebook.
- Verify auger depth calibration at the start of each sampling day.
- Ensure sieve integrity (no torn or damaged mesh) before processing.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                             |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Used gloves             | Standard trash                              |
| Decontamination rinse water | Pour on ground away from sampling plots |
| Coarse fragments        | Return to field site or dispose in trash    |

## Training Record

Before sampling independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Participate in a supervised sampling session
4. Demonstrate proper auger technique, homogenization, and sieving
5. Be signed off by the field lead or PI
